title: QuickCart Flash Sale
description: Scale a stateless request tier behind a load balancer to carry a 1,000,000 req/s flash sale while  keeping every server within an 80% capacity headroom budget.

prompt.text:
You are the backend architect for an e-commerce website called QuickCart.

QuickCart is running a major flash sale. During the sale, the website is expected to receive up to 1,000,000 requests per second.

Each backend server can handle a maximum of 100,000 requests per second. To keep the servers stable, use no more than 80% of each server's capacity.

The load balancer distributes incoming requests evenly across every backend server you add.

Build the backend architecture for QuickCart from available components.
functionalRequirements: Accept incoming user traffic through a load balancer.
Distribute traffic evenly across a pool of backend servers.
Serve the full offered load without dropping requests.

nonFunctionalRequirements.description: Throughput must be at least 1,000,000 req/s.

structuralRules.description: Include a load balancer; either the L4 or L7 subtype is accepted.
Include at least one backend API server.
Connect the traffic source directly to the load balancer.
Connect the load balancer directly to the backend server pool.
Every node must be reachable (no orphans).

cases.description: Sustain the 1,000,000 req/s flash-sale peak within the 80% server headroom budget.

invariants.description: No server may exceed 80% of its capacity during the sale

dryRunCase.description: Try the public flash-sale workload before submitting; hidden grading thresholds are evaluated separately.

checks.description: Keep errors under 1%: drop virtually no requests during the sale.
Serve the full flash-sale load: total throughput reaches 1,000,000 req/s.
Stay within the headroom budget: no server runs above 80% of its capacity.

author: Hritvik Mohan
